title: Chainlog values must be retrieved from multiple independent sources and cross-checked for agreement
content:
A.1.10.2.4.12.2.8 makes Chainlog retrieval mandatory during validation and specifies how: "The most secure method for retrieving values is to query the Chainlog directly using **multiple sources**, such as Foundry's `cast` tool, the Etherscan blockchain explorer, and the IPFS link accessible on the official Chainlog for Sky, **ensuring that the returned addresses match across all platforms**."

The three paths fail differently, which is the whole design. `cast` depends on the validator's RPC endpoint; Etherscan depends on a centralized indexer; the IPFS copy depends on published content and pinning. A compromised RPC could return a plausible but wrong address; a manipulated explorer view could do the same; a stale IPFS record could disagree with both. Agreement across all three is evidence no single one is lying.

This matters because the Chainlog is the name-to-address directory the whole Spell references. A validator who resolves a name to the wrong address will diligently verify a Spell against a fabricated target and find nothing wrong — the check would pass while the underlying assumption is corrupt.

It is the same duplicate-independent-path reasoning applied elsewhere in the Atlas — two Spell Teams agreeing on novel designs, two parties summing transfers, a document hash computed by two tools — extended here to data *retrieval* rather than data production. The recurring principle is that the trustworthiness of an input is established by the diversity of the paths that produce it.
description: A.1.10.2.4.12.2.8 names cast, Etherscan and the IPFS-hosted Chainlog, requiring returned addresses to match across all three so a single compromised source cannot mislead a validator.
